description.narrative:
Focus Area 1: Revamping FDCs as Centres for Training, Innovation, and Community Engagement
KTO's ongoing participation in creating safe spaces for adolescents and youth in FDCs has been strengthened through its active role in the Comprehensive Program for Adolescents and Youth under the Safeguard Young People (SYP) Tanzania initiative, supported by UNFPA. As a key implementer, KTO has been appointed to the SYP Tanzania Country Program Technical Committee.
Through various initiatives and interventions, the FDC concept has been further strengthened across the country. KTO successfully obtained legal registration to operate in Zanzibar, specifically to expand the FDC model to the Isles.
Library management training was successfully completed for 33 principals, librarians, and teachers from 11 FDCs. As a result, participants gained a deeper understanding of the role of government experts in establishing and managing libraries, and successfully applied government guidelines for college and community libraries. The training also led to the development of strategies for implementing college libraries that will serve both FDC participants and the surrounding community
KTO remains an active member of the National Girls' Education Caucus, a collaborative forum consisting of key organizations such as CAMFED, UMATI, FAWE TZ, Haki Elimu, TGNP Mtandao, TAMWA, LHRC, Child Support Tanzania, CDF, and Msichana Initiative. As part of this group, KTO continues to contribute to advancing girls' education, particularly through its participation in the design of re-entry implementation plan that support girls in returning to school after dropping out. This collaboration allows KTO to influence policy and program development aimed at improving educational opportunities for girls across Tanzania through the AEP.
Capacity building in functional literacy was conducted for 7 FDC trainers from 7 different FDCs2. The training included equipping the trainers with methods for teaching illiterate participants. They also learned how to create a practical and technical literacy guide for training instructors in FDCs and developed a guide for this purpose. This training equipped the trainers with effective methods for teaching illiterate participants and focused on developing practical, technical literacy guides tailored for in service training of FDC tutors.

Focus Area 2: Enhancing Gender Equality Lifelong Learning and Human Development through FDCs
The program, carried out in 54 FDCs through a close partnership between KTO and MoEST, focuses on young mothers and women dropped out of school for various reasons. It provides these participants with access to secondary education in a non-formal environment, vocational training, life skills, and entrepreneurship, helping them move into employment and/or continue their education. In 2024, the program recruited 1,166 participants and with established 37 daycare centers being operational with a total of 995 (475 boys and 520 girls) children.
KTOs impacts include restoring hope for young people, particularly those who left school due to pregnancy, by providing targeted training and employment opportunities. The organization has also increased self-awareness and confidence, especially among young mothers, empowering them to become more assertive about their sexual and reproductive health rights. KTO has successfully shifted community perceptions about girls' education, with parents becoming more supportive of continuing education after pregnancy. In addition, the organization has enhanced economic empowerment through vocational and adult education programs. The well-being of participants and FDC staff has improved both mentally and physically. By offering safe daycare options, KTO has enabled young families to have more productive time. Finally, the organization has promoted gender equality and social inclusion, particularly for young mothers.
As of December 2024, a total of 44 FDCs in Tanzania were registered as secondary education examination centers, enabling students to sit for their national exams and further their academic progression. Additionally, 37 daycare centers have been established within 37 FDCs to provide essential childcare services. These centers cater to the children of FDC students and participants, staff members, and families from the surrounding communities. The initiative aims to support parents and guardians, particularly women, by enabling them to participate in educational and vocational training programs without compromising their childcare responsibilities.
Mpira Fursa program, implemented in partnership with the Tanzania Football Federation (TFF), Ministry of Information, Culture, Arts and Sports (MoCAS), and Ministry of Education Science and Technology (MoEST) aims to establish a nationwide framework to promote women's and girls' football. It seeks to identify and empower girls to become skilled and confident football players with a solid understanding of the sport and its economic opportunities. The program also promotes gender awareness and increased participation of girls in sports, while boosting their self-esteem, confidence, and knowledge of their rights.
3. To advance the Adult Education agenda at national, regional, and international levels, KTO continues to actively engage in lobbying and networking efforts.
In October 2022, Grimslövs Folk High School and Sörängens Folk High School, together with five other Swedish folk high schools and fourteen FDCs, launched a collaborative project with a visit to Tanzania. This partnership aims to further the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) from Agenda 2030 by utilizing Atlas Planning from the Swedish Council for Higher Education. The collaboration includes biannual exchanges of principals, teachers, and students through online and in-person meetings to enhance global understanding between Swedish and Tanzanian FDCs. As part of this initiative, Ilula and Katumba FDCs, along with KTO, participated in a learning visit to Grimslövs Folk High School in Sweden. The visit focused on sharing and learning about folk and adult education practices in both countries. The 24 successful visit led to Tanzanian participants sharing insights and recommendations with 54 other FDCs in Tanzania. According to KTO, the collaboration is expected to foster expertise and improve the delivery of folk and adult education in both Sweden and Tanzania.
Through a range of targeted initiatives and strategic interventions, the FDC model has seen considerable reinforcement and expansion across the country. KTO successfully obtained legal authorization to operate in Zanzibar, paving the way for the introduction and growth of the FDC model in the Isles. In addition to securing this formal registration, KTO was able to engage effectively with local authorities, leading to the acquisition of office space to support the launch and coordination of its activities in the Isles. According to KTO these efforts mark a significant step forward in the broader effort to extend the FDC framework and its benefits to new areas, ensuring a solid foundation for future operations.The results are following up the same flow of objectives (what KTO wants to achieve).
